jobs.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one polished editorial illustration for OWNED, a practical book for product and technology leaders working with investors. Landscape 16:9. Match an existing ink-and-color book style: opaque warm ivory paper background (#faf8f2), bold navy outlines (#172b49), muted teal, warm ochre, subtle paper texture, calm adult professional characters and concrete working objects. Flat hand-drawn editorial illustration, not photorealism or 3D. Spacious composition, large high-contrast labels with short line breaks, legible at article width. Only the exact labels requested below; no additional text on notes, screens, books, boards or props. No overall title, figure number, brand, watermark, financial numbers, upward charts, coins or decorative robots. Empty notes and simple unlabeled geometric sketches are allowed. Explain management delivery with board oversight. Two main areas: a board meeting on the left, and a clearly outlined company area on the right. The left vignette shows three board members reviewing a simple plan, labelled "Board". The right area is headed "Company". Inside it, an upper vignette of two company executives reviewing a plan is labelled "Company leaders"; a lower vignette of a product leader and two engineers working with a laptop and product sketch is labelled "Product & engineering". A plain line WITHOUT arrowheads joins the Board only to Company leaders, labelled "Plan & review". Inside the company, a single downward arrow from Company leaders to Product & engineering is labelled "Delivery decisions". A small allocation card beside the delivery team is labelled "Funded capacity". The company boundary must enclose both company vignettes and the allocation card. Make the board and company scenes distinct but equally clear. Do not draw any direct Board-to-engineer line or place board members inside the delivery team. Show actual company work, not an investor commanding every task. Exact labels only: "Board", "Company", "Company leaders", "Product & engineering", "Plan & review", "Delivery decisions", "Funded capacity".
jobs.alt: The board agrees the plan and reviews it with company leaders, who make delivery decisions and allocate funded product and engineering capacity.
jobs.caption: Board oversight works through an agreed plan and review. Company leaders retain delegated delivery decisions and need funded people to carry them out.
